source.check: returned unopposed: 'There are no changes regarding the following eighteen outgoing members who are returned unopposed ...' (Derry Journal 21 May 1952 p2; Londonderry Sentinel 22 May 1952 p2). The list gives names and townlands, not divisions.

note: Triennial election of the 23 electoral divisions of Limavady rural district, one member each, polled on 5 June 1952. Twenty-seven candidates were nominated and four divisions were contested; the Nationalists gained two seats and with them control of the council. Sixteen of the nineteen unopposed members added from the nominations report (Derry Journal, 21 May 1952, p. 2; Londonderry Sentinel, 22 May 1952, p. 2): Ballykelly as the report gives it, the rest from their divisions at the 1949 return. Aghanloo, Feeny and The Highlands (W. J. Thompson, James O'Kane, John Alcorn) are held, as for 1949 (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 2 June 1949 return (recorded from the Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1949, p. 6, with the division of the 1946 return: Denis Farren for Ballyharrigan; Belfast News-Letter, 2 November 1946, p. 5); the Derry Journal of 21 May 1952, p. 2, names the member as an outgoing member returned unopposed. The 1955 nominations list (Derry Journal, 18 May 1955, p. 2) again names him for this division as its retiring member. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Ballyharrigan' to Ballyharigan (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (BALLYHARIGAN) spell it Ballyharigan. This round was filed under the spelling 'Ballyharrigan', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (ballyharrigan) answers with a redirect to this one.
